Package index

Start here — four complete recipes

Copy-and-run examples for the four table shapes a clinical report is mostly made of: demographics, adverse events, PK concentrations and a laboratory shift table. Each runs end to end, data in and RTF out, and they are shown together because their arguments barely overlap – what a demographics table needs, an adverse-events table does not.

rtfreporter-recipes
Four complete recipes: DM, AE, PK and LB

Document & rendering

Start here. rtf_document() creates the document; the section and content calls below add to it; generate_rtfreport() writes the file. Acts on: the rtf_document object. rtf_page() and rtf_default_format() are the only settings that are document-only – everything else in this reference acts on a table. rtf_config() edits an already-composed document; rtf_document() starts a new one.

rtf_document()
Create an RTF document for pipe composition
rtf_config()
Configure document-level settings
rtf_page()
Page geometry for an RTF document
rtf_default_format()
Document-wide default formatting for an RTF document
generate_rtfreport()
Generate an RTF file from a report object
print(<rtf_document>)
Print an rtf_document object
print(<rtfreport>)
Print an rtfreport object

Package defaults

Inspect and reset the rtfreporter.* option defaults (paper size, orientation, margins, font, font size). Acts on: nothing – these set the fallbacks every other function uses when you do not pass a value. A site can set its own in Rprofile.site; see the page-setup article.

rtfreporter_options()
Inspect the active rtfreporter defaults
rtfreporter_reset_defaults()
Restore the factory default options

Sections — headers & footers

A section applies a running header / footer to a range of pages. Acts on: the rtf_document object. Headers and footers are themselves small tables: build their rows with rtf_header() / rtf_footer() and edit one row later with update_header_row() / update_footer_row().

rtf_section()
Define sections for pages
rtf_header() rtf_footer()
Create a header or footer object for a section
update_header_row() update_footer_row()
Update a specific row in an rtf_header() object

Page content — tables & figures

Place a table or a figure on the page, with its titles and footnotes. Acts on: the rtf_document object – rtf_tables() takes the rtftable objects the sections below produce. Note the two levels: rtftable() sets how a table looks; passing the same setting to rtf_tables() overrides it for that placement only, leaving the table object untouched.

rtf_tables()
Add content pages to document
rtf_figures()
Add figure content to document
rtf_titles()
Assign content titles to pages
rtf_footnotes()
Assign content footnotes to pages
rtftable()
Create an RTF table object
rtfplot()
Create an RTF figure object
print(<rtftable>)
Print an rtftable object
format(<rtftable>)
Render an rtftable body as console text
summary(<rtftable>)
Summarise an rtftable object
print(<rtfplot>)
Print an rtfplot object

Importing tables (gt / gtsummary / rtables / rlistings → rtftable)

Turn a table object – a gt::gt() table, a gtsummary table, an rtables/tern VTableTree, an rlistings listing_df, or a plain data.frame – into rtftable objects, reading the source’s metadata and paginating in one call. Acts on: the source object. Produces: rtftable objects. as_rtftables() returns one per page (a list); as_rtftable() returns a single object. stub_cols() prepares a tidy data.frame beforehand by merging hierarchy columns into one indented stub column; stub_spec() carries the same settings into as_rtftables(stub = ).

as_rtftables()
Convert a table object into rtfreporter table pages
as_rtftable()
Convert one table object to a single rtftable
combine_sections()
Combine table page lists into one auto-sectioned list
stub_cols()
Merge hierarchy columns into one indented stub column
stub_spec()
Bundle the row-stub settings for as_rtftables()

Listings (source data → listing body)

Reshape source data into what a listing prints, before any of it is rendered: source variables joined into one printed column, a long cell wrapped over several physical rows, narrow gutter columns, and a blank row after each record. Acts on: a data.frame / tibble. Produces: a data.frame, which as_rtftables() renders. listing_col() describes one printed column and listing_spec() the listing as a whole; build_listing() applies the spec, and as_rtftables(listing = ) runs the same work inside the pipeline and derives the header, the widths and the alignment from it. An rlistings listing_df needs none of this – it is already laid out, and goes straight to as_rtftables(). fit_listing_widths() proposes every column’s width from the page and the data, and listing_code() prints the spec as source to paste and tune. catx() is the join a listing column makes, exported for the columns you build yourself.

listing_col()
One printed column of a listing
listing_spec()
Bundle the settings for one listing
build_listing()
Reshape a data.frame into a listing body
fit_listing_widths()
Propose the listing's column widths from the page and the data
listing_code()
Print a listing spec as the code that would build it
catx()
Join values with a separator, skipping the missing ones

Column headers

Build and edit the column-header block. Acts on: an rtftable – there is no header setting at document level. col_cell() describes one header cell and is accepted by rtf_col_header(), rtftable(col_header = ), rtf_tables(col_header = ) and set_header_cell(). A whole header built with rtf_col_header() goes to the same places plus set_col_header(). Coordinates are those of the finished table, so a merged stub counts as one column.

col_cell()
Column-header cell specification
rtf_col_header()
Build a multi-row column-header specification
col_header_from_names()
Build a spanning column header from delimited column names
add_col_header_row()
Append (or prepend) a row to an rtf_col_header
set_col_header()
Set the whole column header of a finished table (final-table coordinates)
set_header_cell()
Set or merge individual column-header cells (spanning, borders, alignment)
rtf_columns()
Column names of a finished table's body
rtf_header_source()
Deparse a table's column header back to editable rtf_col_header() source

Post-hoc styling verbs

Restyle a table you have already built, without rebuilding it. Acts on: an rtftable, or a list of them – every verb here has a list method, so one call styles every page. These are the last word: they override whatever rtftable() or the source adapter set. set_decimal_split() is the exception in kind – it does not change the data, only how a numeric column is rendered.

style_header() style_cols() style_body() style_zone() add_header_row()
Restyle an existing rtftable (post-hoc styling verbs)
collapse_repeats()
Blank out consecutive repeated values in a finished table
set_decimal_split()
Line up the decimal points of a numeric column

Built-in cell-format functions

Re-shape the TEXT of cells so counts and percentages line up. Acts on: a data.frame or a character vector, before it becomes a table. Pass one to rtftable(cell_format = ) / as_rtftables(cell_format = ) to apply it during the build instead.

format_count_pct()
Format count + percent cells to a uniform display width
realign_count_pct()
Re-align existing "n (xx.x)" strings to a uniform display width
fmt_count_paren()
Align "count (parenthetical)" cells
fmt_count_paren_bare()
Align "count (parenthetical)" cells, including bare counts
fmt_right_align()
Right-align the cells of a column to a common width

Numeric display formatters

Turn numbers into the strings a clinical table prints – significant digits, rounding, alignment. Acts on: a data.frame or a numeric vector, before it becomes a table. Numbers reaching rtftable() unformatted are converted with as.character(), which is rarely what a report wants, so format first.

fmt_signif()
Format numbers to a number of significant digits
fmt_round()
Format numbers to a fixed number of decimal places
fmt_numeric()
Format the numeric columns of a table for display

Blank rows

Insert blank separator rows by position, by value change, or by rule.

set_blank_rows()
Attach blank-row positions to a data.frame
blank_rows_by_change()
Blank-row specification: insert when a variable's value changes
blank_rows_by_rule()
Blank-row specification: insert before/after rows matching a pattern

Pagination strategies & helpers

Split a table across pages. Acts on: the body of a table being built. Vertical splitting is chosen with as_rtftables(split = ) – a strategy name ("group_safe", "group_force", "by_value", "rows", "none") with its settings given as ordinary arguments alongside it, or a function of your own for a bespoke rule. paginate_cols() is the horizontal counterpart: it acts on a FINISHED rtftable, splitting a too-wide table by column and repeating the row headings on every page.

paginate_cols()
Paginate a table horizontally, by columns
add_cont_label()
Prepend a continuation label row to a paginated chunk

Borders

Two constructors, and only two: rtf_border_side() describes one edge – its line style, width and colour – and rtf_border() collects edges into the border of a cell, a row or a zone, including the rules inside a selection (inside_h, inside_v). Where usable: both are accepted by rtftable(border = ), rtf_tables(border = ) and the style_*() verbs; rtf_border() is also accepted by col_cell(border = ). There is no border setting at document level. Later wins, per edge – a style_*() call overrides rtftable(), which overrides the adapter. The constructors these two replaced are listed under Deprecated at the bottom of this page; ?rtf_border pairs the old and the new spelling for every case.

rtf_border_side()
Single-edge border specification
rtf_border() rtf_border_none() rtf_border_top() rtf_border_bottom() rtf_border_box()
Four-edge border specification for a cell or row

Shared table styles (S3, snapshot)

One object carrying borders, alignment, padding and row height, so a set of tables can share a look. Where usable: rtftable(style = ) and rtf_tables(style = ). rtf_table_style_with() derives a variant from an existing style, changing only the fields you name.

rtf_table_style()
Shared table style
rtf_table_style_with()
Return a copy of an rtf_table_style with selected fields replaced
rtf_table_style_tfl()
Clinical TFL preset (table style)

Column-width utilities

Measure text and size columns to their content. Acts on: a data.frame; returns widths in twips for rtftable(column_widths_twips = ). Use auto_col_widths() when long labels wrap; as_rtftables(auto_width = TRUE) does the same during the build, clamped to the writable page width.

text_width_in()
Estimate the display width of a text string
auto_col_widths()
Automatically calculate column widths for a data.frame

Visual preview (S3 plot methods)

Look at a table, a border or a document without writing a file. Acts on: whichever object you pass; nothing is modified. These are for checking work in progress, not for producing output.

Assembling multiple RTF files

Join finished RTF FILES into one, with a table of contents and continuous page numbering. Acts on: files on disk, not R objects – this is the step after generate_rtfreport(). A spec (assemble_spec(), a .csv/.xlsx) names the files and their TOC entries.

assemble_files()
Collect the RTF files in a folder
assemble_folder()
Assemble every RTF in a folder into one TOC deliverable
assemble_spec()
Build an assembly spec (one editable row per RTF)
assemble_from_spec()
Assemble RTF files from an assembly spec
assemble_toc()
Build a TOC definition from a set of RTF files
toc_heading()
Build a structured TOC heading
toc_entry()
Build a structured TOC entry

Post-processing

Edit a rendered RTF file in place – substituting text a report needs only at delivery time, such as a run date or a draft watermark. Acts on: a file on disk.

rtf_replace_text()
Replace text inside a generated RTF file

Superseded

Still working and not scheduled for removal: newer work goes into the replacement each page names, but existing code need not change.

paginate()
Split a table object into per-page data.frames (deprecated)

Deprecated – scheduled for removal

The border constructors that rtf_border_side() and rtf_border() replaced at 0.5.0 / 0.6.0. They still work and each warns once per session, naming its replacement, but they will be removed in one batch before the CRAN submission – do not write new code against them. ?rtf_border pairs the old and the new spelling for every case. rtf_border_none(), rtf_border_top(), rtf_border_bottom() and rtf_border_box() are documented on the rtf_border() page itself.

rtf_border_with()
Return a copy of an rtf_border with selected sides replaced
rtf_table_border()
Per-zone border specification for a table
rtf_border_tfl()
Clinical TFL-style table border preset
